subject: NexaCare MSA / Order Form — DPA redlines & SCCs coordination
messages:
From: Sara Morales <sara.morales@nexacare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: NexaCare MSA / Order Form — DPA redlines and SCCs

Hi Kimberly / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at NexaCare has a few substantive redlines to the DPA and a couple of requests around cross‑border routing and SCCs that we need to get tied to the MSA/order form before procurement can push to DocuSign. I’ve attached our consolidated redline (NexaCare_DPA_Redline_20261108.docx). High level:

- We want Redwood to accept Processor role only; controller statements need to be clear that NexaCare is the controller.
- We propose a Transfer Impact Addendum that routes EU‑origin traffic to EU regions first and falls back to US hosting only if EU capacity is unavailable. We added language allowing exceptions for backups/DR; please confirm.
- SCCs: we started with the standard EU SCC template but made two edits related to subcontractor approval and subprocessor audit rights (see §4 and §7).

Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood is comfortable with the proposed routing fallback language and the limited exceptions?
2) Whether you can provide SOC2 (most recent) and a KMS architecture diagram for the record?
3) Target timeline for redline resolution and final signature — procurement wants a tentative date.

We’d like to get a final DPA attached to the order form and in DocuSign ideally before 2026‑11‑18. Happy to take a call if faster.

Attachments: NexaCare_DPA_Redline_20261108.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Sara Morales
Senior Counsel, NexaCare

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara.morales@nexacare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NexaCare MSA / Order Form — DPA redlines and SCCs

Sara — thanks, appreciate the consolidated redline. I’ve triaged this with ops and legal and outlined a quick mutual action plan below.

Internal owners (for NexaCare):
- Ben Carter (Legal Ops) — lead on contract redlines and indemnity/loss language; will produce first pass redline.
- Marissa Cole (Security) — will gather SOC2 + KMS diagram and confirm technical feasibility for KMS in VPC.
- Laura Bennett (Privacy) — will review SCC edits and proposed subprocessor audit language.

Proposed MAP / timeline:
- 2026‑11‑12: Internal first‑pass DPA redline ready from Redwood legal (Ben).
- 2026‑11‑14: Share Redwood redline back to NexaCare legal with inline comments.
- 2026‑11‑15 or 11‑16: Joint call to resolve open issues (can do 11/15 10:00 PT — please confirm).
- Target DocuSign: by 2026‑11‑18 if we close the call quickly.

Two quick clarifying asks now:
1) On the routing fallback, do you require a contractual SLA for EU region availability or is “best effort with notification” acceptable?
2) The SCC edits you propose — are those mandatory edits from your compliance group or negotiable?

I’ve attached a short triage note for internal use; Ben will take the lead on legal redlines.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_initial_review_notes.txt]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Morales <sara.morales@nexacare.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NexaCare MSA / Order Form — DPA redlines and SCCs

Kim / Sara — I started a line‑by‑line pass. Initial flags (high level):
- Indemnity / liability: NexaCare redline expands controller liability into processor obligations for certain transfers — we need to push back or carve for limited transfer exceptions.
- Training data / retention: there’s a proposed retention window tied to “retraining use” that is too broad for our policy; we’ll propose narrower language and a separate data retention schedule in the Order Form.

Request: can you attach the latest Order Form (the one with pricing and module list)? will help tie the DPA exhibits.

I attached my working comments (ben_redline_comments.pdf). I’ll aim to send a consolidated Redwood redline by 2026‑11‑12 EOD.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ben_redline_comments.pdf]

From: Sara Morales <sara.morales@nexacare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NexaCare MSA / Order Form — DPA redlines & SCCs

Ben — thanks for the quick review. I’ve attached the Order Form we expect to sign (NexaCare_OrderForm_v3.pdf). A few replies inline:

- Controller/Processor: NexaCare will remain controller; Redwood should be processor. The indemnity point is about third‑party liabilities arising from data exports — we can be pragmatic about carveouts.
- Routing fallback: NexaCare’s compliance team prefers a contractual routing preference for EU origin traffic with fallback to US only if EU capacity is unavailable; they asked for a notification window (48 hours) before fallback.
- SCCs edits are requested by our privacy counsel; they’re not optional on our side, so please treat §4 and §7 edits as required.

We can do a call 2026‑11‑15 10:00 PT — I’ll pencil that in. Procurement is pushing for signature by 2026‑11‑18 but expects some give and take.

Attachments: NexaCare_OrderForm_v3.pdf

— Sara

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Morales <sara.morales@nexacare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 07:56:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: NexaCare MSA / Order Form — DPA redlines & SCCs

Sara — quick answers from privacy/ops side ahead of the call:

- Processor role: fine — we’ll add a clarifying recital and make sure the exhibits map responsibilities.
- SCCs: we can accept the SCC framework but need to limit NexaCare’s requested subprocessor audit rights to a security‑approved schedule (we can propose an access window and redaction rules).
- Routing fallback / TIA: acceptable in principle. We propose the following compromise:
  * Contract language will state Redwood routes EU origin traffic to EU regions as priority.
  * Fallback to non‑EU hosting only when EU region capacity is unavailable for >48 hours OR for temporary peak bursts for which capacity can’t be scheduled.
  * Exclude backups/DR copies from the routing restriction (these may replicate to the US).

Evidence / items we will provide before the call:
- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) — redacted version for procurement.
- KMS architecture diagram (ops network view) — sanitized for external sharing.

Action items for the 11/15 call (10:00 PT):
- Ben to walk through the indemnity carveouts and retention schedule suggestion.
- Kim to confirm the Order Form modules we need to tie to the DPA exhibits.
- Marissa to present KMS diagram and confirm whether customer‑managed keys are supported on VPC/private deployments.

If the call goes well we should be able to finalise the DPA addendum language and target DocuSign 11/18.

Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
